entities.text: High Court Of Judicature At Allahabad, Lucknow Bench
entities.label: COURT

sentences.text:
Case :- Application U/S 482 No. - 6065 of 2015
Applicant :- Dinesh Maurya

Opposite Party :- State Of U.P. And Anr.
Counsel for Applicant :- Sandeep Kumar Srivastava
Counsel for Opposite Party :- Govt. Advocate
Hon'ble Om Prakash Shukla,J.
1.

Heard learned Counsel for the applicant and Shri Arvind Kumar Tripathi, learned Additional
Government Advocate for the State and perused the record.

3. Learned Counsel for the applicant has submitted that the applicant has been falsely implicated in
the aforesaid case as he has not committed any offence as alleged in Case Crime No. 438 of 2015.
4.  Learned AGA has submitted that this petition under Section 482 Cr.P.C. is not maintainable as the applicant has got efficacious remedy by filing discharge application.

5. Taking into consideration the fact that the applicant is having an equally efficacious remedy to file discharge application before the competent Court, without entering into the merits of the issue, the Dinesh Maurya vs State Of U.P. And Anr. on 13 August, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/52814492/

entities.text: Dinesh Maurya vs State Of U.P. And Anr
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text:
1 applicant is permitted to file a discharge application before the trial Court through counsel taking all pleas and grounds, which are available to him, enclosing therewith the relevant documents/evidence, which are necessary for disposal of the discharge application, within a period of four weeks from today and if such application is filed by the applicant before the trial Court within the aforesaid stipulated time, the trial Court shall consider and decide the said application strictly in accordance with law, by speaking and reasoned order and by affording an opportunity of hearing to the concerned parties, expeditiously, say within a period of two weeks thereafter.
6. Till disposal of such discharge application, applicant may not be compelled to appear before the court below in the aforesaid case, but it is made clear that if the present applicant does not file any discharge application within the aforesaid stipulated time, i.e. within a period of four weeks from today, the benefit of this order shall not be extended to the applicant.
7. The application is, accordingly, disposed of.
( Om Prakash Shukla, J.) Order Date :- 13.8.2024 Ajit  Dinesh Maurya vs State Of U.P. And Anr. on 13 August, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/52814492/
